docs.text: Silverlight360.UnRAR ¶ Extracts RAR archives on the Xbox 360's own drives from a Silverlight360 app. UnRAR 7.3.2's library, built with xsdk into a DLL of its own, unrar360.xex , does the reading, decompressing and writing natively; the app passes paths and watches progress through RarExtractor . using (var rar = new RarExtractor()) { // On a thread of its own: Extract returns when the archive is done. int result = rar.Extract(@"hdd:\Downloads\game.part1.rar", @"hdd:\Games\Game", null); if (result != RarExtractor.Success) Show(RarExtractor.Describe(result) + ": " + rar.Message); } Paths are the console's, as xsdk names its drives: hdd:\ the hard disk's data partition, usb:\ (or usb0: to usb2: ) the USB drives, game:\ the app's own folder. The archive never passes through managed memory, so its size doesn't matter. An app's own code runs interpreted on the console, and decompressing in C# would be far too slow ( Silverlight360's Performance ). RAR5 and RAR4 archives, stored, solid, encrypted and split into volumes, are extracted; a 61 MB archive of a 75 MB package takes under a second in xenia-edge. Getting it ¶ A release has what an app needs, built: unrar360.xex The DLL, at base 0x8F000000 Silverlight360.UnRAR.dll , Silverlight360.UnRAR.xml The C# side, RarExtractor , with its documentation for IntelliSense. It needs Silverlight360.Common, which an app built with Silverlight360 has licenses/unrar.txt , THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md UnRAR's license, which goes with the DLL LICENSE.md , README.md , BUILD.txt Silverlight360.UnRAR's license, and what the release was built from Then see Adding it to an app . To build it yourself, see Building . Where it runs ¶ In xenia-edge , where every check of the sample passes, and on a console (retail kernel 2.0.17559, running unsigned code), where the DLL loads in a Silverlight app's process beside Silverlight360.Https . See Testing for what was checked where.

Returns Success or one of UnRAR's ERAR_ codes (below) void Cancel() From another thread: stops the extraction at its next block of data; Extract returns 21 int FilesDone Entries extracted so far, folders among them long BytesDone Bytes written so far string CurrentFile The file being extracted, or the last string Message What went wrong, after an Extract that didn't return Success : the file and UnRAR's error static string Describe(int code) A code's meaning, as "wrong password" void Dispose() Frees the extractor's progress buffer The DLL, for all extractors: const uint DefaultHeapBytes 128 MB: the heap Extract starts the DLL with if Start hasn't static void Start(uint heapBytes) Starts the DLL with a heap of up to heapBytes , reserved now and committed as it's used; once static uint Version The wrapper's API version, then UnRAR's library version, 16 bits each static uint HeapCommitted , static uint HeapPeak The DLL's heap in use now, and the most it has held at once: what to size Start by Codes ¶ Code Success 0 Extracted 11 Not enough memory: the archive's dictionary doesn't fit the heap 12, 13 Damaged data, or a damaged archive 14 Unknown format 15 Can't open the archive 16, 17 Can't create or close a file, such as a name over FATX's 42 characters 18, 19 Read or write error 21 Stopped ( Cancel ), or an unknown error MissingPassword 22 The archive is encrypted and no password was given BadPassword 24 Wrong password 25 Dictionary too large

docs.text: Building ¶ The DLL builds in WSL (or on Linux) with xsdk's toolchain. Clone it, then set up the rest, in PowerShell: git clone https://github.com/Digiex/Silverlight360.UnRAR.git cd Silverlight360.UnRAR .\tools\Configure.ps1 Configure.ps1 gets what the build needs, each the way that suits it: UnRAR's source UnRAR 7.3.2, which RARLAB publishes only as a tarball unrarsrc-7.3.2.tar.gz downloaded from rarlab.com into third_party\ , checked against its SHA-256, and unpacked into third_party\unrar ; git ignores both. Another version is a change of $unrarVersion and $unrarSha256 in the script xsdk jessenic/xsdk , branch dll-modules , the build XboxNGen uses: its elf2xex.py has --dll , and its build/libxsdk.a is what the DLL links Found from -Xsdk , XSDK , XboxNGen's configuration beside this repository, or a checkout two folders up ( C:\Proj\xsdk ) or beside it; otherwise cloned two folders up, if you say so. libxsdk.a is built if it isn't xsdk's toolchain GCC 15.3, binutils and newlib for powerpc-xsdk-elf , in WSL Found in ~/xsdk-gcc or at -Toolchain ; otherwise built there with xsdk's tools/toolchain/build.sh , if you say so: about 10 minutes, and a 136 MB download of their sources Silverlight360 The SDK, for Silverlight360.UnRAR.dll and the sample Found from -Silverlight360 , its environment variable, or a checkout beside this repository; otherwise cloned there, if you say so It also checks WSL has make , cmake , ninja , python3 and git ( sudo apt install build-essential cmake ninja-build python3 git in Debian). -NonInteractive asks nothing: -CloneXsdk , -BuildToolchain and -CloneSilverlight360 say what it may fetch or build. It writes config.mk ( XSDK and TOOLCHAIN as WSL sees them, for the Makefile), config.props (for the C# projects) and config.json (for tools\Release.ps1 ); git ignores them, and -Show prints them. Then, in WSL, in the repository's folder: make -j$(nproc) That writes unrar360.xex (750 KB). UnRAR's source is built as it comes, with src/compat.h included ahead of it for what xsdk lacks, so it isn't modified. make clean starts over; the Makefile's XSDK , TOOLCHAIN and ELF2XEX can be given on its command line to build with something else. Silverlight360.UnRAR.dll ¶ The C# side builds as a Silverlight360 class library, in PowerShell, with Silverlight360 where .\tools\Configure.ps1 -Show says (here beside this repository, as XboxSilverlightSdk ): ..\XboxSilverlightSdk\tools\Build-XboxApp.ps1 -Project .\csharp\Silverlight360.UnRAR.csproj That writes csharp\bin\Release\Silverlight360.UnRAR.dll and Silverlight360.UnRAR.xml , its documentation for IntelliSense, with Silverlight360.Common.dll , which it references, beside them. The sample ¶ sample/ is a Silverlight360 app that extracts each test archive and checks the result: ..\XboxSilverlightSdk\tools\Build-XboxApp.ps1 -Project .\sample\UnRarSample.csproj See Testing for running it.

docs.text: Contributing ¶ Bug reports, fixes and improvements are welcome on GitHub . Say what you're changing in an issue first if it's more than a small fix, so the work isn't done twice. Run .\tools\Configure.ps1 , build it ( Building ) and run the sample's checks in xenia-edge ( Testing ). A change to the DLL's loading, its memory or its layout should be tried on a console too, with the DLL probed first. Keep UnRAR's source as it comes: what xsdk lacks goes in src/compat.h and src/posix.c , not in a change to the source. A move to a newer UnRAR is a change of the version and SHA-256 in tools\Configure.ps1 . Keep RarExtractor.cs building for Silverlight 3's C#, and the API in API up to date with what it has. Open a pull request against master . The docs site is built for it, so a broken link shows before the merge. Don't send code or files from the Xbox 360 SDK, or from projects whose licenses don't allow it. License ¶ Silverlight360.UnRAR is licensed under the PolyForm Noncommercial License 1.0.0 with an additional condition. By opening a pull request, you agree that your contribution is licensed under the same terms.

docs.text: Development ¶ What's here ¶ src/extract.cpp The DLL's extraction API, on UnRAR's own library interface ( dll.hpp ) src/runtime.c , src/runtime.h The C and C++ runtime xsdk's title start would set up, set up by unrar360_init instead, with a bounded heap src/posix.c , src/compat.h The POSIX calls UnRAR's Unix build makes that xsdk doesn't have src/export.h UNRAR360_EXPORT , which gives a function an ordinal for elf2xex unrar360.ld , Makefile The DLL's layout, at base 0x8F000000 , and its build third_party/unrar UnRAR's source, which tools\Configure.ps1 fetches (git ignores it) csharp/RarExtractor.cs The C# side: DllImport s by ordinal, and progress read from a pinned buffer csharp/Silverlight360.UnRAR.csproj Builds it as Silverlight360.UnRAR.dll , a Silverlight360 class library, with its XML documentation sample/ A Silverlight360 app that extracts each test archive and checks the result tests/ The test archives' maker, and a check of what the sample extracted tools/Configure.ps1 , tools/Config.ps1 Sets up the build ( Building ), and reads what it saved tools/Release.ps1 Builds a release and publishes it on GitHub docs/ , mkdocs.yml This site The C side and the C# side share the layout of the progress buffer ( src/extract.cpp , and the offsets at the top of RarExtractor.cs ), big-endian; a change to one is a change to both. The exports are by ordinal, #1 to #5 : the UNRAR360_EXPORT lines in the sources, and the DllImport s. Releasing ¶ .\tools\Release.ps1 -DryRun # builds and zips, shows the notes, publishes nothing .\tools\Release.ps1 # 0.1.0 first, then the last release's patch raised .\tools\Release.ps1 -Bump Minor As Silverdash360's and Silverlight360.Https's release scripts do: The release is made from the commit as it is: nothing may be uncommitted, and the commit must be on GitHub already. Nothing is pushed. The version is -Version if given, else the last release's (the highest v<version> tag) with its patch, or -Bump 's part, raised. It's tagged v<version> on the commit, by gh . The DLL is built from scratch in WSL ( make clean , then make ), with what tools\Configure.ps1 set up. Silverlight360.UnRAR.dll and Silverlight360.UnRAR.xml are built from csharp\Silverlight360.UnRAR.csproj by Silverlight360's tools\Build-XboxApp.ps1 , so a release needs Silverlight360 configured. Silverlight360.UnRAR-<version>.zip , in build\release , has in a Silverlight360.UnRAR folder unrar360.xex , Silverlight360.UnRAR.dll , Silverlight360.UnRAR.xml , README.md , LICENSE.md , THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md , licenses\ and BUILD.txt , which records the commits of Silverlight360.UnRAR and xsdk it was built from, UnRAR's version, and the toolchain. The release's notes are the commits since the last release, and the zip is its file. It needs the GitHub CLI ( gh ), signed in, unless -DryRun . Test a build before releasing it ( Testing ): the script builds it, it doesn't run it. The docs ¶ This site is the docs folder, built with MkDocs ( mkdocs.yml ). A push to master that changes it publishes it to GitHub Pages ( .github/workflows/docs.yml ). To preview it: pip install mkdocs==1.6.1 python -m mkdocs serve

docs.text: Licenses ¶ Silverlight360.UnRAR itself, its C and C++ code, RarExtractor.cs , its build and its documentation, is licensed under the PolyForm Noncommercial License 1.0.0 with an additional condition: any project made with it must include a visible reference to https://github.com/Digiex/Silverlight360.UnRAR in its documentation, credits or "about" information. A project made with it includes an app shipped with unrar360.xex or Silverlight360.UnRAR.dll . See LICENSE.md . unrar360.xex is built from UnRAR's source, which keeps its own license, by Alexander Roshal: licenses/unrar.txt , with THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md . An app that ships the DLL ships that license with it; a release has it in its licenses folder. In short, it: allows using UnRAR's source to handle RAR archives in any software, free of charge; doesn't allow using it to make a RAR-compatible archiver, or to recreate RAR's compression; asks that a modified copy of the source keep its second paragraph, the one starting "UnRAR source code", in the license or documentation and in the source's comments. This project doesn't modify the source: it's built as it comes, with src/compat.h included ahead of it. The repository doesn't hold UnRAR's source: tools\Configure.ps1 downloads it from rarlab.com, checked against its SHA-256.

docs.text: Limits ¶ FATX names. The console's file system takes names of up to 42 characters; an archive holding longer ones fails at that file with "can't create a file". No file times or owners. xsdk has no utimensat or lchown , so extracted files keep the time they were written. The read-only attribute is set, through xsdk's chmod . One thread. UnRAR's own threads ( RAR_SMP ) are left out; the console has six hardware threads to try them on. Memory. The heap is reserved up front (128 MB unless Start says otherwise) and committed as used. An archive whose dictionary doesn't fit fails with "not enough memory". RAR5's dictionaries go up to 4 GB and RAR7's further. A fatal error in the DLL (an abort ) stops the extraction's thread for good rather than the app, and the log says why: there's no way to end only the DLL. The log is the host title's, default.log in game:\ , where game: can be written. One base address. The DLL is linked at 0x8F000000 , one of the bases free in a Silverlight app's process on the console; another DLL in the same app needs another. Extracting only. UnRAR's license allows handling RAR archives, not making them (see Licenses ).
docs.title: Limits

docs.text: Testing ¶ In xenia-edge ¶ .\tests\make_archives.ps1 -ContentRoot $env:TEMP\unrar-content -Work $env:TEMP\unrar-tree -Large path\to\large.rar ..\XboxSilverlightSdk\tools\Test-XboxApp.ps1 -Xex .\sample\bin\Release\xbox\default.xex -Output $env:TEMP\unrar-run ` -ExtraArgs "--content_root=$env:TEMP\unrar-content" -Seconds 60 python tests\verify_output.py $env:TEMP\unrar-tree\manifest.json $env:TEMP\unrar-content\UnRarTest\out ` 0-rar5 1-rar4 2-store 3-solid 4-password 5-split.part1 make_archives.ps1 writes a 5 MB test tree and archives it six ways with WinRAR's Rar.exe , and copies -Large , any large archive, in as large.rar . xenia-edge's hard disk is its content folder, hdd:\Content , so the archives go in <content root>\UnRarTest\in and come out in UnRarTest\out . The log has a PASS: or FAIL: line for each case. Clear out between runs: xenia-edge shows a folder in a content-type folder that holds one file, as a package's .data folder can, as that one file, so a second run can't write into it. What passed in xenia-edge, 2026-11-07, with the DLL at 0x8F000000 , built against xsdk's dll-modules libxsdk.a : RAR5, RAR4, stored, solid, encrypted and split archives of the 5 MB tree, every file matching its hash ( verify_output.py ); a missing archive and a wrong password, with their codes; a 61 MB archive of a 75 MB Games on Demand package in 871 ms, and cancelling it after 16 MB; the heap peaked at 8.4 MB. On 2026-11-02, at the old base, the large archive also came out byte for byte as WinRAR extracts it. On a console ¶ Before an app calls a new build, check that the console loads it: a DllImport of a module that can't load turns into a call through null, which can power the console off. The CLR loads a DllImport module as GAME:\<name> with XexLoadImage flags 9; Silverdash360's debug server does the same with xex.probe GAME:\unrar360.xex 9 , then unloads it. What ran on a console, 2026-11-07 (retail kernel 2.0.17559, running unsigned code): XexLoadImage loaded the DLL at 0x8F000000 (status 0) in Silverdash360's process, with Silverlight360.Https's DLL loaded at 0x8D000000 . The first build, at 0x8C000000 , couldn't have: that base is taken in a Silverlight app's process there. An extraction on a console hasn't been run yet.

The log has a PASS: or FAIL: line for each case. Clear out between runs: xenia-edge shows a folder in a content-type folder that holds one file, as a package's .data folder can, as that one file, so a second run can't write into it. docs.text: Adding it to an app ¶ An app needs the C# side and the DLL beside default.xex : Silverlight360.UnRAR.dll , RarExtractor , with Silverlight360.UnRAR.xml beside it for IntelliSense: a reference to the release's DLL, or a ProjectReference to the repository's csharp/Silverlight360.UnRAR.csproj . unrar360.xex , as Content . The C# side uses NativeBuffer from Silverlight360's common library , Silverlight360.Common, for the progress the DLL writes. An app built with Silverlight360 references that library already, and its build puts Silverlight360.Common.dll in the package. In the app's project, as sample/UnRarSample.csproj has them: <ItemGroup> <ProjectReference Include="..\Silverlight360.UnRAR\csharp\Silverlight360.UnRAR.csproj" /> <!-- or, from a release: <Reference Include="Silverlight360.UnRAR"><HintPath>..\Silverlight360.UnRAR\Silverlight360.UnRAR.dll</HintPath></Reference> --> </ItemGroup> <ItemGroup> <Content Include="..\Silverlight360.UnRAR\unrar360.xex"><Link>unrar360.xex</Link></Content> </ItemGroup> Ship the release's licenses/unrar.txt and THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md with them: unrar360.xex is built from UnRAR's source, under its own license. Silverlight360.UnRAR's own license asks for a visible reference to https://github.com/Digiex/Silverlight360.UnRAR in the app's documentation, credits or "about" information (see Licenses ). Extracting ¶ Extract blocks until the archive is done, so call it on a thread of its own, never the UI's, and read the progress from the UI's: var rar = new RarExtractor(); ThreadPool.QueueUserWorkItem(delegate { int result = rar.Extract(@"usb:\Downloads\movie.rar", @"hdd:\Videos\Movie", null); Deployment.Current.Dispatcher.BeginInvoke(() => Show(result == RarExtractor.Success ? "Done" : RarExtractor.Describe(result) + ": " + rar.Message)); rar.Dispose(); }); // On a timer on the UI thread: Status.Text = rar.FilesDone + " files, " + rar.BytesDone / (1 << 20) + " MB: " + rar.CurrentFile; One extraction at a time per extractor. Cancel , FilesDone , BytesDone and CurrentFile are for other threads. Folders are kept as the archive has them, and those missing are made. A split archive's other volumes must be beside the first. A password goes to Extract ; a wrong one returns BadPassword , and none for an encrypted archive MissingPassword . The first extraction starts the DLL with a heap of DefaultHeapBytes (128 MB, reserved and committed as it's used): RAR5's 32 MB dictionary and more. Call RarExtractor.Start(bytes) before the first one for another size; HeapPeak says what an extraction needed (8.4 MB for the test archives). The DLL loads at 0x8F000000 . In a Silverlight app's process on the console, 0x8A000000 , 0x8C000000 and 0x8E000000 are taken and Silverlight360.Https has 0x8D000000 , so another DLL of the app's own needs a base of its own. A DllImport of a module that can't load turns into a call through null, which can power the console off, so check a new build loads first (see Testing ). See API for everything an extractor has.
